decision: Do not promote the external format or checkpoint change to production. Lower software I/O and faster sequential reads do not establish a large-write win; small-file and aged-read tradeoffs remain.
scope: Isolated C++ Linux external-payload and checkpoint coalescing prototypes

plan.scope: Isolated Linux hybrid external-payload prototype. Independent 4 KiB logical blocks; full 64-block vacant-range batches go to an append file. Small and occupied writes retain inline SQLite payloads. No production default or migration change.
plan.durability: Append bytes fdatasync before SQLite reference commit, even in fsync mode. GC FULL metadata commit before hole punching; shared native transaction guards exclude concurrent physical reclamation.
plan.selection: Compare total I/O, fresh and aged reads/writes, small-file/metadata behavior, GC and recovery before promotion. Preserve baseline settings, all samples and outliers.

followup_plan.hypothesis: The hybrid layout adds 256 data barriers; the original total-WAL wake condition causes roughly 160 background database syncs per 256 MiB write. Gate new checkpoints on 16 MiB uncopied WAL bytes; preserve existing unfinished-checkpoint retry and 64 MiB total-WAL admission. Keep all durable ordering and GC unchanged.
followup_plan.comparison: fresh paired baseline/coalesced runs after first experiment and related correctness tests finish; retain initial external experiment in full
